# v1.0.7 — the metadata now matches the archive

Version 1.0.6 added the script behind Supplementary Table S28 and retitled the
Zenodo record, but three files inside the package still described the previous
study. This version fixes only those; no script, estimate or exhibit changed.

## What was wrong

- `CITATION.cff` carried the pre-revision title and `version: 1.0.5`. GitHub's
  "Cite this repository" and the Zenodo record both read that file, so the
  citation the archive surfaced was for the wrong paper.
- `DATA_AVAILABILITY.md` quoted the manuscript's availability statement as it
  stood in version 1.0.5, pinned to the DOI of that version
  (`10.5281/zenodo.23750085`). A file inside a release cannot name its own
  version DOI without going stale on the next one.
- The descriptive sentence in `.zenodo.json` still read "…a cohort study of
  two-year agreement in low grip strength classification and the incremental
  prognostic value of an earlier reading", the pre-revision framing.

## What changed

- `CITATION.cff`: title updated to the revised manuscript, `version: 1.0.7`.
- `DATA_AVAILABILITY.md`: the quoted statement now cites the concept DOI
  (`10.5281/zenodo.23677282`, which resolves to the latest version) and names the
  version described, so it stays correct across versions.
- `.zenodo.json`: descriptive sentence rewritten to match the revised study;
  `version` set to `v1.0.7`.

## Where the analysis lives

The S28 script is unchanged from 1.0.6:
`code/charls_only/97_s28_dominant_2025.R`. Run it against `out/jamda_full.rds`
and the CHARLS release under `_x/`; it writes `out/S28_dominant_2025.csv`. At
ages 50–64 the dominant-hand rule classifies 2.5 percentage points more
participants as low (ratio 1.19, 95% CI 1.9–3.1) and two-year reversion is 2.3
points lower (ratio 0.96, 95% CI −4.8 to 0.3); the direction of the paper's
conclusion is unchanged.

Version 1.0.6 remains citable as `10.5281/zenodo.23917161`. Cite this version,
or the concept DOI, which resolves here.
